_readme: Every reference used anywhere in the tool. `provenance` records where each citation came from: `prior_project` = researched in the Khazan project (STEP_PROMPT_hazard_science.md / elements.json) and carried over; `build_spec` = named in docs/COASTAL_DRR_TOOL_BUILD_PROMPT.md; `this_pass` = added in this build from the literature as known to the author, NOT yet checked against the source document. The UI labels this_pass citations as 'to verify'. `checked_this_pass` = read against the source document itself in this build.

mcivor2012_waves.full: McIvor, A.L., Möller, I., Spencer, T. & Spalding, M. (2012). Reduction of wind and swell waves by mangroves. Natural Coastal Protection Series: Report 1. Cambridge Coastal Research Unit Working Paper 40. The Nature Conservancy and Wetlands International.
mcivor2012_waves.usedFor: Mangrove wave-height reduction of 13–66% per 100 m of mangrove belt.

mazda1997.full: Mazda, Y., Magi, M., Kogo, M. & Hong, P.N. (1997). Mangroves as a coastal protection from waves in the Tong King delta, Vietnam. Mangroves and Salt Marshes 1: 127–135.
mazda1997.usedFor: Field measurements underlying the McIvor et al. (2012a) wave-attenuation range.

mazda2006.full: Mazda, Y., Magi, M., Ikeda, Y., Kurokawa, T. & Asano, T. (2006). Wave reduction in a mangrove forest dominated by Sonneratia sp. Wetlands Ecology and Management 14: 365–378.
mazda2006.usedFor: Field measurements underlying the McIvor et al. (2012a) wave-attenuation range.

mcivor2012_surge.full: McIvor, A.L., Spencer, T., Möller, I. & Spalding, M. (2012). Storm surge reduction by mangroves. Natural Coastal Protection Series: Report 2. Cambridge Coastal Research Unit Working Paper 41. The Nature Conservancy and Wetlands International.
mcivor2012_surge.usedFor: Mangrove reduction of peak storm-surge water level, reported as roughly 4–48 cm per km of mangrove width.

goda2010.full: Goda, Y. (2010). Random Seas and Design of Maritime Structures, 3rd edition. Advanced Series on Ocean Engineering, Vol. 33. World Scientific.

usace_cem.full: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (2002, with later updates). Coastal Engineering Manual. Engineer Manual EM 1110-2-1100 (Part VI: Design of Coastal Project Elements). Washington, DC.
usace_cem.usedFor: Seawall reflection behaviour and failure once overtopped/breached; dune design framework.

fema_coastal_structures_2024.full: FEMA (2024, November). Guidance for Flood Risk Analysis and Mapping: Coastal Structures. Federal Emergency Management Agency.
fema_coastal_structures_2024.usedFor: Framework for treating dunes and coastal structures in flood-risk analysis.

fema_540_rule.full: FEMA. Guidance for Flood Risk Analysis and Mapping: Coastal Erosion — the "540 square foot rule": a frontal dune with less than 540 ft² (≈50.2 m²) of cross-sectional area above the 1%-annual-chance stillwater elevation is assumed to be removed during the base flood; one with at least that area is assumed to be retained (eroded by retreat). Criterion traces to FEMA's 1988 dune-erosion methodology.
fema_540_rule.usedFor: Dune retained-vs-removed test by cross-sectional volume.

njseagrant_dune.full: New Jersey Sea Grant Consortium. Dune engineering / management manual (as named in the build spec; edition and authors to be confirmed).
njseagrant_dune.usedFor: Dune design framework (not used for any number).

dangremond1996.full: d'Angremond, K., van der Meer, J.W. & de Jong, R.J. (1996). Wave transmission at low-crested structures. Proceedings of the 25th International Conference on Coastal Engineering (Coastal Engineering 1996), ASCE, pp. 2418–2427.
dangremond1996.usedFor: Wave transmission coefficient range for low-crested/detached breakwaters (Kt ≈ 0.075–0.8).

fema_p946.full: FEMA (2013). Federal Guidelines for Inundation Mapping of Flood Risks Associated with Dam Incidents and Failures. FEMA P-946.
fema_p946.usedFor: Framework for store-and-release and breach behaviour of small dams (not used for any number).

usace_em1110_2_1420.full: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (1997). Hydrologic Engineering Requirements for Reservoirs. Engineer Manual EM 1110-2-1420.
usace_em1110_2_1420.usedFor: Framework for reservoir flood-storage accounting (not used for any number).

naro_paddy_dam.full: National Agriculture and Food Research Organization (NARO), Japan, and Japan Society of Civil Engineers (JSCE) literature on paddy-field-dam flood mitigation, as assembled in the prior Khazan project (STEP_PROMPT_hazard_science.md §4). A representative study: Yoshikawa, N., Nagao, N. & Misawa, S. (2010). Evaluation of the flood mitigation effect of a Paddy Field Dam project. Agricultural Water Management 97(2): 259–270. Specific source for the 1,000–2,000 m³/ha figure still to be pinned.
naro_paddy_dam.usedFor: Order-of-magnitude flood-storage headroom of bunded paddy/wetland, ~1,000–2,000 m³ per hectare.

wahl2015.full: Wahl, T., Jain, S., Bender, J., Meyers, S.D. & Luther, M.E. (2015). Increasing risk of compound flooding from storm surge and rainfall for major US cities. Nature Climate Change 5: 1093–1097.
wahl2015.usedFor: Compound surge + rainfall/fluvial flooding as a dependent, worse-than-either event.

moftakhari2017.full: Moftakhari, H.R., Salvadori, G., AghaKouchak, A., Sanders, B.F. & Matthew, R.A. (2017). Compounding effects of sea level rise and fluvial flooding. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 114(37): 9785–9790.
moftakhari2017.usedFor: Compound coastal + fluvial flooding in estuaries.

sendai2015.full: UNISDR (2015). Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015–2030. United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction, Geneva.
sendai2015.usedFor: Risk as a function of hazard, exposure and vulnerability.

ipcc_ar6_wg2.full: IPCC (2022). Climate Change 2022: Impacts, Adaptation and Vulnerability. Contribution of Working Group II to the Sixth Assessment Report. Cambridge University Press. In particular Chapter 3 (Oceans and Coastal Ecosystems and their Services; Cooley et al.), Figure 3.24 and Table 3.SM.3, and Cross-Chapter Paper 2 (Cities and Settlements by the Sea; Glavovic et al.).
ipcc_ar6_wg2.usedFor: Risk framing; separate feasibility and effectiveness assessment of coastal adaptation options.

singh2020.full: Singh, C., Ford, J., Ley, D., Bazaz, A. & Revi, A. (2020). Assessing the feasibility of adaptation options: methodological advancements and directions for climate adaptation research and practice. Climatic Change 162: 255–277.
singh2020.usedFor: Feasibility dimensions used in the feasibility × effectiveness view.

iucn2020.full: IUCN (2020). IUCN Global Standard for Nature-based Solutions: a user-friendly framework for the verification, design and scaling up of NbS. First edition. Gland, Switzerland: IUCN.
iucn2020.usedFor: Eight-criterion checklist shown for every nature-based or hybrid solution.

invest_cv.full: Natural Capital Project. InVEST User's Guide: Coastal Vulnerability model. Stanford University, University of Minnesota, The Nature Conservancy and WWF.
invest_cv.usedFor: Methodology precedent: a transparent, formula-based index combining physical variables, with the formula shown.

czmp_goa.full: National Centre for Sustainable Coastal Management (NCSCM), MoEF&CC, for the Department of Environment & Climate Change, Government of Goa. Coastal Zone Management Plan (CZMP), Goa, prepared under the CRZ Notification 2011; mapped period 2017–2022; 1:25,000.
czmp_goa.usedFor: CRZ classification of the Panjim pilot area (all CRZ areas and the map layer).

crz2011.full: Ministry of Environment and Forests, Government of India (2011). Coastal Regulation Zone Notification, 2011. S.O. 19(E), 6 January 2011.
crz2011.usedFor: Definitions of the CRZ categories (CRZ-I to CRZ-IV, the 0–200 m No Development Zone).

huizinga2017.full: Huizinga, J., de Moel, H. & Szewczyk, W. (2017). Global flood depth-damage functions: Methodology and the database with guidelines. JRC Technical Report EUR 28552 EN. Publications Office of the European Union. doi:10.2760/16510. Database: copy_of_global_flood_depth-damage_functions__30102017.xlsx, publications.jrc.ec.europa.eu/repository/handle/JRC105688, downloaded 23 Oct 2026.
huizinga2017.usedFor: Depth-damage functions (Asia: residential, commercial, industrial, roads, agriculture) and India's maximum damage values, for damage in INR (audit M12, Phase 2).

shetye2007.full: Shetye, S.R., Dileep Kumar, M. & Shankar, D. (eds) (2007). The Mandovi and Zuari Estuaries. National Institute of Oceanography, Goa.
shetye2007.usedFor: Named as the calibration route for surge/tide and river-flood propagation along the Mandovi (not used for any number).

sandrp_goa.full: South Asia Network on Dams, Rivers and People (SANDRP). Goa river profile (as gathered in the prior Khazan project; exact title and date to be confirmed).

lwm_khazan.full: Living Waters Museum. Documentation of Goa's khazan bund-and-sluice system (as gathered in the prior Khazan project; exact page to be confirmed).
lwm_khazan.usedFor: Context on the khazan system as the illustrative tidal-wetland / polder hybrid.

ipcc_ar6_wg1_slr.full: Fox-Kemper, B., Hewitt, H.T., Xiao, C., et al. (2021). Ocean, Cryosphere and Sea Level Change. In: Climate Change 2021: The Physical Science Basis. Contribution of Working Group I to the Sixth Assessment Report of the IPCC, Chapter 9 (GMSL projections, Table 9.9), Cambridge University Press; with the WG1 Summary for Policymakers (B.5.3). Also used in the AR6 Synthesis Report (2023).
ipcc_ar6_wg1_slr.usedFor: Global mean sea-level rise by 2050 and 2100 under SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5, relative to 1995–2014 (median and likely range).

copernicus_glo30.full: European Space Agency / Airbus (2021, 2022 release). Copernicus DEM GLO-30: global 1 arc-second Digital Surface Model, heights relative to the EGM2008 geoid. Copernicus Programme; accessed via the AWS Open Data registry (s3://copernicus-dem-30m), tile N15 E073.
copernicus_glo30.usedFor: Ground (surface) elevation for the bathtub-fill inundation extents.

ipcc_ar6_wg2_ch3_smtable.short: IPCC AR6 WGII Ch3 SM, Table SM3.3
ipcc_ar6_wg2_ch3_smtable.full: IPCC (2022). Chapter 3 Supplementary Material (Cooley, S. et al., Oceans and Coastal Ecosystems and their Services), Table SM3.3: Background materials and data for Figures 3.23 and 3.24, including the full feasibility assessment (pp. SM3-36 to SM3-43). In: Climate Change 2022: Impacts, Adaptation and Vulnerability, Working Group II contribution to the Sixth Assessment Report. Final Draft (accepted version). Feasibility is assessed in three paired dimensions (technical & economic; institutional & geophysical; socio-ecological), each High / Medium / Low, plus general feasibility and effectiveness (High / Medium / Low).
ipcc_ar6_wg2_ch3_smtable.usedFor: Feasibility rating scale (High / Medium / Low), the wording of the feasibility rubric (adapted from the table's per-option justifications), and the global reference ratings shown for 'Habitat restoration' and 'Protection & beach and shore nourishment'.

sundar2005.full: Sundar, D. & Shetye, S.R. (2005). Tides in the Mandovi and Zuari estuaries, Goa, west coast of India. Journal of Earth System Science 114(5): 493–503. doi:10.1007/BF02702025.
sundar2005.usedFor: Tidal range in the Mandovi and Zuari increases by about 20% up to ~45 km from the mouth, then drops sharply near the upstream end (tide-pole records at 13 stations, March–April 2003): evidence that a near-zero decay of surge level along the channel is the right direction of simplification.

ramakrishnan2022.full: Ramakrishnan, R., Remya, P.G., Mandal, A., Mohanty, P., Arayakandy, P., Mahendra, R.S. & Nair, T.M.B. (2022). Wave induced coastal flooding along the southwest coast of India during tropical cyclone Tauktae. Scientific Reports 12: 19966. doi:10.1038/s41598-022-24557-z.
ramakrishnan2022.usedFor: Analog for an extreme-event coastal water level on this coast: at Chellanam (Kerala) during Cyclone Tauktae (2021), infragravity waves plus wave setup raised coastal water elevation to about 1.5 m, while the forecast storm surge there was only about 0.15 m.

ipcc_ar6_wg2_ccb_feasib.full: IPCC (2022). Cross-Chapter Box FEASIB: Feasibility Assessment of Adaptation Options: An Update of the SR1.5, in Chapter 18 (Climate Resilient Development Pathways) of Climate Change 2022: Impacts, Adaptation and Vulnerability, Working Group II contribution to the Sixth Assessment Report; Figure Cross-Chapter Box FEASIB.2. Each option is assessed across six dimensions (economic, technological, institutional, socio-cultural, environmental, geophysical), each as high, medium or low feasibility, or limited evidence / no evidence (LE/NE).
ipcc_ar6_wg2_ccb_feasib.usedFor: The feasibility rubric's structure: the six dimensions and the High / Medium / Low / LE/NE rating states.

esri_elevation.full: Esri (2026). ArcGIS Elevation service, /elevation/at-many-points (ArcGIS Location Platform), TopoBathy elevation at the best resolution available. Sources at Panjim per the WorldElevation/Terrain mosaic catalogue: Airbus WorldDEM4Ortho 24 m and 74 m, SRTM 1 arc-second, EarthEnv-DEM90, GMTED2010. Queried 2026-09-27.
esri_elevation.usedFor: Independent cross-check of the Copernicus GLO-30 heights (not used in the model: not finer here; see the DEM grounding note).

esri_places.full: Esri (2026). ArcGIS Places service, /places/within-extent (ArcGIS Location Platform); places data based on Foursquare Open Source Places. Categories: Hospital; Primary and Secondary School; Fire Station; Police Station; Government Building; Town Hall. Queried live; results are not stored (Places terms of use).
esri_places.usedFor: Optional critical-facilities map layer (hospitals, schools, fire and police stations, government buildings) shown against the selected flood extent. Coverage in Panjim is incomplete.

census2011_panaji.full: Census of India (2011). Panaji (M Corp. + OG), North Goa, Goa: population 70,991 (Panaji Municipal Corporation alone: 40,017), listed across 37 wards and out-growth units including Taleigao (24,201). Compiled at census2011.co.in/data/town/803243-panaji-goa.html (a secondary compilation of Census of India 2011 town data).
census2011_panaji.usedFor: Population exposure: the 70,991 total allocated to the four segments by their share of in-scope land area.

mpt_tor_2016_tides.full: Mormugao Port Trust (2016). Capital dredging of the approach channel and berths at Mormugao Port: Form I and draft Terms of Reference, Rev. 00, Section 2.3.1 Tides (p. 6), quoting Indian Naval Hydrographic Chart No. 2020: tide levels w.r.t. chart datum at Mormugao Harbour: higher high water at spring +2.3 m, mean higher high water +1.9 m, mean lower high water +1.8 m, mean higher low water +1.0 m, mean lower low water +0.5 m, mean sea level +1.3 m. environmentclearance.nic.in/writereaddata/Online/TOR/21_Sep_2016_185740063Y7IXR73WCapital_dredging_MPT_Rev00.pdf (accessed 22 Oct 2026).
mpt_tor_2016_tides.usedFor: High-tide reference: MHHW +0.6 m above MSL (default), spring HHW +1.0 m (top of range).

eurotop2018.full: Van der Meer, J.W., Allsop, N.W.H., Bruce, T., De Rouck, J., Kortenhaus, A., Pullen, T., Schüttrumpf, H., Troch, P. & Zanuttigh, B. (2018). EurOtop: Manual on wave overtopping of sea defences and related structures. An overtopping manual largely based on European research, but for worldwide application. 2nd edition. www.overtopping-manual.com (accessed 22 Oct 2026).
eurotop2018.usedFor: Seawalls and dunes act by crest height: they hold still water below the crest and are overtopped above it. Reflection does not lower the still-water level behind a wall.

muis2020_codec.full: Muis, S., Irazoqui Apecechea, M., Dullaart, J., de Lima Rego, J., Madsen, K.S., Su, J., Yan, K. & Verlaan, M. (2020). A high-resolution global dataset of extreme sea levels, tides, and storm surges, including future projections. Frontiers in Marine Science 7:263. https://doi.org/10.3389/fmars.2020.00263. Data: CoDEC Dataset, Zenodo, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.3660927 (CC BY 4.0; file CODEC_amax_ERA5_1979_2017_coor_mask_GUM_RPS.nc, accessed 22 Oct 2026).
muis2020_codec.usedFor: Storm-tide (tide + surge) return levels at the Mandovi mouth, GTSM point id_coast_glob_12128.

ar6_slr_tool.short: NASA/IPCC AR6 Sea Level Projection Tool
ar6_slr_tool.full: Garner, G.G., Hermans, T., Kopp, R.E., Slangen, A.B.A., Edwards, T.L., Levermann, A., Nowicki, S., Palmer, M.D., Smith, C., Fox-Kemper, B., et al. (2021). IPCC AR6 Sea Level Projections, version 20210809. Zenodo, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.5914709. Accessed through the NASA Sea Level Projection Tool, https://sealevel.nasa.gov/ipcc-ar6-sea-level-projection-tool?psmsl_id=1249 (Mormugao, PSMSL 1249), 22 Oct 2026.
ar6_slr_tool.usedFor: Relative sea-level rise at Mormugao by 2050 and 2100 for SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5 (median and likely range).

vafeidis2019.full: Vafeidis, A.T., Schuerch, M., Wolff, C., Spencer, T., Merkens, J.L., Hinkel, J., Lincke, D., Brown, S. & Nicholls, R.J. (2019). Water-level attenuation in global-scale assessments of exposure to coastal flooding: a sensitivity analysis. Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences 19, 973-984. https://doi.org/10.5194/nhess-19-973-2019
vafeidis2019.usedFor: Overland water-level attenuation range, 0 to 1.0 m/km (storm-driven water only).

pronk2024_deltadtm.full: Pronk, M., Hooijer, A., Eilander, D., Haag, A., de Jong, T., Vousdoukas, M., Vernimmen, R., Ledoux, H. & Eleveld, M. (2024). DeltaDTM: A global coastal digital terrain model. Scientific Data 11: 273. doi:10.1038/s41597-024-03091-9. Data: DeltaDTM v1.1, 4TU.ResearchData, doi:10.4121/21997565 (CC BY 4.0); the Mandovi tile was supplied by Ferdin (23 Oct 2026) because 4TU was unreachable. Produced using Copernicus WorldDEM-30 (c) DLR e.V. 2010-2014 and (c) Airbus Defence and Space GmbH 2014-2018 provided under COPERNICUS by the European Union and ESA.
pronk2024_deltadtm.usedFor: Terrain model (audit M8): bare-earth heights below 10 m, replacing the GLO-30 surface model; GLO-30 fills cells above 10 m and water.

ghs_pop_2023.full: Schiavina, M., Freire, S., Carioli, A. & MacManus, K. (2023). GHS-POP R2023A - GHS population grid multitemporal (1975-2030). European Commission, Joint Research Centre (JRC). doi:10.2905/2FF68A52-5B5B-4A22-8F40-C41DA8332CFE. CC BY 4.0. Epoch 2020, 3 arc-second, tile R8_C26, downloaded 23 Oct 2026 from jeodpp.jrc.ec.europa.eu.
ghs_pop_2023.usedFor: People per grid cell (exposure, people affected), replacing the uniform spread of the census total (audit Phase 2, P2.1).

osm_buildings.full: OpenStreetMap contributors (2026). Building footprints, roads, landuse and creek geometry in the Panjim window, via the Overpass API (overpass-api.de), fetched 23 Oct 2026. Open Database License (ODbL) 1.0.
osm_buildings.usedFor: Building footprints and use class, road surfaces, farmland, creek outlets for the rain catchments.

ms_buildings.full: Microsoft (2026). Global ML Building Footprints, India, release 2026-02-03 (quadkeys 123303002, 123303003), github.com/microsoft/GlobalMLBuildingFootprints. Open Database License (ODbL). Downloaded 23 Oct 2026.
ms_buildings.usedFor: Buildings missing from OpenStreetMap (13,909 of 18,802 footprints in the window). Used instead of Google Open Buildings, whose tile for Goa is 4.8 GB.

datameet_villages.full: DataMeet (2016-). Indian Village Boundaries: Goa (ga.geojson), github.com/datameet/indian_village_boundaries, Census 2001 codes. ODbL. Downloaded 23 Oct 2026.
datameet_villages.usedFor: Census town/village each grid cell lies in, for the social vulnerability index.

census2011_pca_units.short: Census of India 2011 PCA (towns near Panaji)
census2011_pca_units.full: Office of the Registrar General & Census Commissioner, India (2011). Primary Census Abstract, as compiled by Brinkhoff, T., City Population (citypopulation.de), pages for Panaji (M Corp. + OG), Calapor, Chimbel and Bambolim, accessed 23 Oct 2026: population, literacy (age 7+) and activity status (age 7+). censusindia.gov.in itself refused the connection (revoked TLS certificate) on 23 Oct 2026.
census2011_pca_units.usedFor: Social vulnerability indicators per census unit; census check on GHS-POP.

worldbank_fx_deflator.full: World Bank (2026). World Development Indicators via api.worldbank.org: PA.NUS.FCRF (official exchange rate, LCU per US$, period average) for India and the Euro area, and NY.GDP.DEFL.ZS (GDP deflator) for India. Accessed 23 Oct 2026.
worldbank_fx_deflator.usedFor: Converting the JRC maximum damage values (EUR, 2010 prices) to INR at 2024 prices.

imd_gridded_rain.short: IMD 0.25 deg gridded rainfall (Pai et al. 2014)
imd_gridded_rain.full: Pai, D.S., Rajeevan, M., Sreejith, O.P., Mukhopadhyay, B. & Satbha, N.S. (2014). Development of a new high spatial resolution (0.25 x 0.25 degree) long period (1901-2010) daily gridded rainfall data set over India and its comparison with existing data sets over the region. MAUSAM 65(1): 1-18. doi:10.54302/mausam.v65i1.851. Data: IMD Pune, imdpune.gov.in/cmpg/Griddata/Rainfall_25_Bin.html, years 1975-2024 downloaded 23 Oct 2026.
imd_gridded_rain.usedFor: Annual maximum 1-day rainfall at the cell over Panjim; Gumbel return levels for the rain-at-high-tide hazard (audit M15).

mccuen2017.full: McCuen, R.H. (2017). Hydrologic Analysis and Design, 4th edition. Pearson. Rational-method runoff coefficients as tabulated in the Minnesota Stormwater Manual, 'Runoff coefficients for different soil groups and slopes' (stormwater.pca.state.mn.us), accessed 23 Oct 2026.
mccuen2017.usedFor: Runoff coefficients for built and unbuilt ground in the rain-at-high-tide volume balance.

gomantak2023_flood.full: Rodrigues, A. (2023, 22 June). Will Smart City Panjim flood or will not, this monsoon? Gomantak Times. gomantaktimes.com/news/goa/will-smart-city-panjim-flood-or-will-not-this-monsoon. Accessed 23 Oct 2026.
gomantak2023_flood.usedFor: Panjim's flood mechanism (heavy rain at high tide, outfalls submerged, about 15-20 such days a monsoon; water from Altinho); Mala pumps (3 x 300 HP + 2 x 60 HP), Mala lake as a retention basin. Press source quoting city engineers.

goa_dip_2023_mala.full: Department of Information & Publicity, Government of Goa (2023, 5 July). CM inaugurates flood water pumping station (DI/NB/AXP/AS/2023/770). goa.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/CM-INAUGURATES-FLOOD-WATER-PUMPING-STATION-.pdf. Accessed 23 Oct 2026.
goa_dip_2023_mala.usedFor: Mala flood-water pumping station: cost about Rs 15.90 crore; drains the Altinho catchment into Mala lake; two actuator gates close at high tide.

ibtracs_v4.full: Knapp, K.R., Kruk, M.C., Levinson, D.H., Diamond, H.J. & Neumann, C.J. (2010). The International Best Track Archive for Climate Stewardship (IBTrACS). Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society 91: 363-376. doi:10.1175/2009BAMS2755.1. Data: IBTrACS v04r01, North Indian basin CSV, NOAA NCEI, downloaded 23 Oct 2026.
ibtracs_v4.usedFor: Compound-event timing check (audit M16): months of cyclonic storms passing near Goa.

schuerch2018.full: Schuerch, M., Spencer, T., Temmerman, S., Kirwan, M.L., Wolff, C., Lincke, D., McOwen, C.J., Pickering, M.D., Reef, R., Vafeidis, A.T., Hinkel, J., Nicholls, R.J. & Brown, S. (2018). Future response of global coastal wetlands to sea-level rise. Nature 561: 231-234. doi:10.1038/s41586-018-0476-5.
schuerch2018.usedFor: Mangrove squeeze indicator: wetlands keep pace with sea-level rise where they have landward accommodation space; barriers and development remove it.

pontee2013.full: Pontee, N. (2013). Defining coastal squeeze: a discussion. Ocean & Coastal Management 84: 204-207. doi:10.1016/j.ocecoaman.2013.07.010.
pontee2013.usedFor: Definition of coastal squeeze (intertidal habitat lost where landward migration is blocked by fixed structures).

drr_audit_2026.full: Coastal Resilience Studio: DRR Tool Review and Model Audit (22 October 2026), docs/DRR_Tool_Review_and_Model_Audit_2026-10-22.docx, Sections 5-6 (findings M1-M18; metric chain).
drr_audit_2026.usedFor: Metric chain and the 0.15 m people-affected convention (stated there as a convention, not a standard).

cutter2003.full: Cutter, S.L., Boruff, B.J. & Shirley, W.L. (2003). Social vulnerability to environmental hazards. Social Science Quarterly 84(2): 242-261. doi:10.1111/1540-6237.8402002.
cutter2003.usedFor: Choice of social vulnerability indicators (education, dependants, livelihood security) and the additive z-score index.

ferdin2026_field_bunds.full: Field knowledge, Ferdin, OneEarth Foundation, 23 Oct 2026: Patto and Taleigao fields are bunded; the St Inez / Merces fields east of 73.848 E are bunded too (same day). Personal communication recorded in docs/STEP_PROMPT_model_p3_accuracy.md and docs/model-audit/LOG.md (Phase 3).
ferdin2026_field_bunds.usedFor: Treating the low fields at Patto, Taleigao and St Inez / Merces (outside the CZMP khazan mask) as bund-protected land (audit A1, Phase 3).

gadm41.full: GADM (2022). Database of Global Administrative Areas, version 4.1 (gadm41_IND shapefiles, release 2022-07-19). University of California, Davis. https://gadm.org. Licence: free for academic and other non-commercial use; redistribution requires permission (https://gadm.org/license.html).
gadm41.usedFor: State, district and taluka boundaries of Goa (data/national/boundaries), as used in the approved mockups; supplied by Ferdin on 2026-11-04.

osm.full: OpenStreetMap contributors (2026). OpenStreetMap data, via the Overpass API (admin relations, creeks, building footprints) and Nominatim (landmark positions, queried 2026-11-04). Open Database Licence (ODbL) 1.0. https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright
osm.usedFor: Landmark positions behind the placeholder ward zones; creeks; administrative relation tags; building footprints in the exposure grid.
